candidates.text: The system must allow each team to manage its own budget, including income (e.g., ticket sales, player sales, property sales) and expenses (e.g., salaries, maintenance).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly describes income and expense categories and clarifies that each team manages its own budget.

candidates.text: The system must enable the IFA to define budget policies and alert when a violation occurs.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder states the IFA should set budget policies and that the system can alert of violations.

candidates.text: The system must allow the IFA administrative to view all transactions across teams for monitoring and auditing.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder says the IFA can see diverse transactions and view entire monetary information.

candidates.text: The system must allow referees to insert game events (e.g., goals, offsides, red cards, player replacements) in real time using a mobile device.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly requests referees to record events in real time via mobile phone.

candidates.text: The system must ensure that only referees can update game events to guarantee data reliability.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder emphasizes that only the referee can update events to avoid unauthorized data.

candidates.text: The system must allow unregistered guests to view final game data (e.g., results, statistics) to promote transparency.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder says even guests can see final game data to increase transparency.

candidates.text: The system must support automatic scheduling of matches based on configurable policies (e.g., home-and-away, minimum gap between matches, day of week).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder describes desired scheduling policies and constraints that the system should enforce.

candidates.text: The system must allow the IFA to manually override the automatic schedule with a rationale, requiring approval from another IFA representative.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explains manual override with justification and dual approval for transparency.

candidates.text: The system must allow the IFA to define policies for assigning referees to games (e.g., avoid same referee for same team, equal distribution of games).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder wants policy-based referee allocation to ensure fairness.

candidates.text: The system must allow referees to input their availability preferences (e.g., vacation days) to be considered in scheduling.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly mentions referees setting preferences like vacation.

candidates.text: The system must allow fans to subscribe to notifications about specific games, teams, or players and receive push notifications (e.g., schedule changes, player posts, live events).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder describes fan subscription to specific interests and push notifications.

candidates.text: The system must provide a fan portal with sections for following players/teams, live updates (including referee reports and scores), and overall tournament rankings.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder agrees with the proposed fan portal structure.

candidates.text: The system must allow players to update their own social network pages within the fan portal.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder says players can update their social network page in the system.

candidates.text: The system must support user registration for all stakeholders (teams, referees, fans) with unique identification, while guests can access public game data.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder mentions registration for identification and guest access.

candidates.text: The system must allow team managers to register their team with the IFA by submitting valid documents, after which the IFA approves and the team can manage its resources.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder describes the team registration process.

candidates.text: The system must allow teams to enter and manage player details, with the IFA only auditing the process.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder says teams enter player details and IFA audits.

candidates.text: The system must allow the IFA to define leagues and seasons, and to register referees.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder lists these as core IFA functions.

candidates.text: The system must keep all past archives of schedules and game data to support future analysis (e.g., for gambling insights).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly requests keeping past archives.

candidates.text: The system must send automatic reminder notifications to team managers for submitting annual reports to the IFA.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder agrees to auto reminders for annual report submission.

candidates.text: The system must allow fans to configure custom alerts, such as a reminder five minutes before a game starts.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder suggests fans can set alerts like pre-game reminders.

candidates.text: The system must support simultaneous access by up to 50,000 users with a response time of 1–2 seconds for fans, IFA admin, and team admin.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states 50,000 concurrent users and reasonable response time.

candidates.text: The system must provide real-time, high-priority responsiveness for referees during games, with immediate event updates.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder emphasizes referee real-time updates with priority.

candidates.text: The system must be developed as a unified system with different interfaces for various stakeholders (web for IFA/teams, mobile app for referees/fans).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder prefers a single system with tailored interfaces.

candidates.text: The system must support localization features including language, currency, and time zone adjustments to serve a global audience.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder raises localization as a key requirement.

candidates.text: The system must comply with data residency regulations, e.g., German data must not leave Germany, requiring flexible data center allocation.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly mentions legal data restrictions.

candidates.text: The system must encrypt budget data to prevent leakage, as it is confidential.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder says budget data should be encrypted.

candidates.text: The system must be fully outsourced for development and maintenance, with the IFA IT department acting as the communication interface.
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder states outsourcing of entire development and maintenance.

candidates.text: The system must be deployed in phases: first phase (basic setup: teams, leagues, seasons, referee/fan registration), second phase (budget and scheduling), third phase (real-time referee updates).
candidates.rationale: The stakeholder outlines a phased implementation sequence.
